summary: Refresh expiring BMW OAuth credentials safely across CLI and typed MCP processes while keeping dry-run and verifier paths offline and refusing live provider calls under local-only mode; resolve config symlinks to one write and lock target, migrate only same-account legacy alias-side streaming sessions to a shared target-side location, check streaming ID-token expiry, clear shadowing legacy auth headers, report archive persistence failures, decode BMW charging fields for local analysis, and restrict unauthenticated MCP HTTP to resolved loopback listeners.
reason: Single-use refresh tokens need a shared file lock and atomic credential writes to the resolved config target; previews and local-only reads must not rotate them, and local-only mode must refuse generated writes, cursor-resetting sync/archive, import, tail and direct streaming. Alias and target users need one streaming session, but one OAuth client ID may serve different accounts, so migration and cleanup require matching saved tokens and account identity. Stale streaming ID tokens must not be reused. A saved legacy auth header can shadow fresh OAuth credentials. Silent archive write failures imply missing data was imported, raw charging field names produce empty local analytics, and non-loopback HTTP would expose credentialed MCP tools.
